memos.scout:
The strongest honest case for buying is thin, and I don't think it clears the base rates.

The one bullish signal is breadth: 782 buyers in the last 15 minutes, 374 buyers in the first two minutes post-graduation, and a top-5 buyer share of only 34.6%, so the early flow wasn't just a few wallets. Pool depth of 143.5 SOL is also reasonable for a $20 ticket.

But the rest points against it. Net flow over the last 15 minutes is negative (-4.5 SOL), sellers (397) outnumber the flow, and the sell-to-buy ratio of 0.77 is weak. Price is down 23.6% from the 30-minute high and 10% over 30 minutes. The curve shows bundle_share of 1.0 and top-3 share of 85%, which suggests coordinated early accumulation rather than organic demand, and a launch bot was present. The "ORGANIC" class label is not enough to override that.

A $20 round trip also costs 1.4-5.1% before any move, and the brief gives no evidence that demand will hold 30-60 minutes out. The honest call is to skip. I'd reconsider only if net flow turned clearly positive over several minutes and the drawdown stopped deepening.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss path: a slow distribution by early holders, not a sudden rug. Net flow over the last 15 minutes is -4.5 SOL, with 134.8 SOL sold against 130.3 bought, and the price is down 9.6% in that window and 23.6% off the 30-minute high. Sellers (397) are roughly half the buyers (782), and the sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes after graduation was 0.77. The curve data points the same way: bundle share is 1.0, top-3 share is 0.85, and the completer share exceeds 1, which suggests early-supply wallets are exiting into retail demand. Against a $20 ticket, a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost leaves little room, and the 46-20% base-rate losses for this kind of setup argue for skipping. Pass.
